Hyngran has accusative experiencer and no expressed nominative. Ðyncan has dative experiencer plus overt singular neuter stimulus and gōd. Neither is expanded into arbitrary persons/content clauses.

Relational versus governed genitive, internal versus external case, recipient/governed/beneficiary/experiencer dative, and ān/sum/hwilc/fela count groups are explicit; no micel mass or general advanced syntax is inferred.
Hīeran perception, tōgelǣdan recipient, wyrcean work, dōn beneficiary, tōtwǣman animals, visit accusative and two on idioms are explicitly taught rather than inferred from familiar headwords.

Cook-selected genēosianē, scęncanę, Crīstī, gātā/ǣ, retained/syncopated stems, dental contractions and reference spelling variants are preserved. Derived cells combine checked lexemes with cited rules, not invented attestation.

No substantive witness error found. Sind/sindon, īdlu/ǣmtig, prospective present versus volitional willan, open command/addressee number and natural reading translation differences are defensible alternatives. Exact-target tasks are separately enforced.
